主要内容: General Electric Company announced on April 10, 2015, its plan to dispose of most of its financial services assets, including selling a substantial majority of GECC's Real Estate debt and equity portfolio to Blackstone Group and a portion to Wells Fargo & Company for a total value of approximately $26.5 billion. The U.S. public indentures of GECC are being amended to provide a full and unconditional guarantee by GE, covering approximately $210 billion of GECC debt. The Company estimates it will incur approximately $23 billion in after-tax charges through 2016, with about $16 billion expected in the first quarter of 2015, including tax expenses, asset impairments, and charges on businesses held for sale. The plan is subject to regulatory review and approval, with the goal of terminating the Financial Stability Oversight Council's designation of GECC as a systemically important financial institution (SIFI). The text also mentions potential challenges in completing the Synchrony Financial split-off and the impact of macroeconomic factors on financial performance and credit defaults.
